audit_summary: Archetype helpers are sound but under-tested at boundaries; H3a RAG is production-wired with silent failure, zero unit tests, global caches, and per-commit subprocess storms — experiment observability and maintainability debt must be tracked before V3.

findings.title: Silent exception swallow hides H3a failures from logs and eval forensics
findings.description: The H3a injection block wraps import + get_historical_defect_context() in `except Exception: pass` with no logging. historical_rag.py logs some internal failures, but import errors, unexpected bugs, and any exception raised after partial work are invisible. During n=50 evals this is indistinguishable from intentional graceful degradation (None return), so D3 attribution to H3a is unreliable and regressions ship silently.
findings.fix: Replace bare pass with `logger.warning("H3a historical context unavailable: %s", exc, exc_info=True)` at debug or warning level. Append a missing_reason when hist_ctx is None after csv_features present (e.g. 'Historical defect priors unavailable'). Never swallow without a trace.

findings.title: New H3a module has zero unit tests on a live prompt-injection path
findings.description: historical_rag.py is wired into every build_investigation_messages() call when csv_features exist, yet no tests/test_historical_rag.py exists and test_hypothesis_engine.py has no assertion for '## Historical Context'. Untested paths include: _load_training_data (missing CSV, corrupt row), _extract_metrics edge cases, KNN neighbor selection, _MIN_CLASSIFIED_FOR_KNN fallback trigger, _get_project_distribution sampling, _classify_message for all 9 categories, subprocess git failures, and repos_base autodetection.
findings.fix: Add tests/test_historical_rag.py with inline CSV fixtures and mocked subprocess.run. Cover: metric extraction, classification, KNN ordering with synthetic rows, fallback when fetched < 3, and get_historical_defect_context returning None vs formatted markdown. Add one integration test in test_hypothesis_engine.py asserting Historical Context section when mock returns data.

findings.title: Process-level mutable singletons break test isolation and block retry
findings.description: _TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED permanently caches failed loads as empty list — a transient CSV read error disables H3a for the process lifetime with no retry. _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE grows unbounded per project key. Parallel pytest-xdist workers would each reload CSV independently (acceptable) but same-worker test order can inherit stale caches; no reset fixture exists. Injected repos_base cannot bypass globals without module reload.
findings.fix: Extract a HistoricalDefectLookup class holding cache state, injectable in tests. Add pytest autouse fixture to reset module globals or use instance-scoped cache. Allow _load_training_data to retry when cache is empty and load failed (distinguish 'attempted empty' from 'file missing').

findings.title: O(n) full-corpus scan plus up to 110 uncached git subprocess calls per commit
findings.description: Each investigation sorts the entire buggy training corpus (potentially tens of thousands of rows) by Euclidean distance, then runs subprocess.run(['git','log',...]) for K=10 neighbors and up to 100 more during project-level fallback — all without message caching. On n=50 eval this adds minutes of I/O latency and timeout risk (5s per call cap × many calls). Side effects in the hypothesis message assembly hot path violate hexagonal expectations.
findings.fix: Pre-index training rows by project at load time; use heapq.nlargest(k) instead of full sort. Cache commit_id→message in an LRU dict keyed by (repo, commit_id). Defer project distribution to one-time startup precompute written to disk. Consider feature flag to disable H3a for timing-sensitive gates.

findings.title: Confirmed typo: \borderring\b never matches 'ordering'
findings.description: The lifecycle-ordering regex contains `\borderring\b` — a misspelling of 'ordering'. This subpattern is dead code and never matches real commit messages. Mitigation: other branches (`\blifecycle\b`, `start.*order`, `stop.*order`, `\bphase\b`) still catch many lifecycle commits, but messages mentioning only 'ordering' or 'bean ordering' without those tokens are misclassified or dropped from priors.
findings.fix: Replace `\borderring\b` with `\bordering\b`. Add a unit test: _classify_message('fix bean ordering on startup') → 'lifecycle-ordering'.

findings.title: Mixed test+prod defect_signals assertion is vacuously true
findings.description: The test asserts has_production_defect_signals(ctx) is False with comment '# no signals in diff', but the diff contains only rsSize literal changes — no guard, lifecycle, or concurrency patterns. This does not prove the test-only guard correctly defers when production files are touched alongside test files. A mixed commit with guard removal in production hunks should still return True — that behavior is untested.
findings.fix: Keep existing assertion but add test_mixed_test_and_prod_still_flags_defect_signals: same mixed touched_files with guard-removal diff in production path; assert has_production_defect_signals is True and detect_archetype is False.

findings.title: H3a always attempted with no feature flag despite minimal measured D3 lift
findings.description: H3a runs unconditionally whenever csv_features is populated — no --enable-h3a flag or env gate. state.json completion_note records 'Net D3 impact minimal (+0.01 ± 0.03)' yet the code path adds latency and subprocess side effects on every commit. Cannot A/B or disable without code change, complicating forensics when D3 regresses.
findings.fix: Add explicit opt-in via run_eval.py flag (mirroring --enable-contrastive pattern) defaulting False until re-validated. Log when enabled and when context injected vs skipped.

findings.title: Git subprocess failures swallowed without logging
findings.description: _get_commit_message catches TimeoutExpired and OSError with bare pass. When local repos are sparse (~14% hit rate per builder note), silent failures make it impossible to distinguish 'commit not in repo' from 'git timeout' from 'repo path wrong' without strace. Compounds TD-001 outer swallow.
findings.fix: Log at debug: logger.debug('H3a: git log failed for %s in %s: %s', commit_id, repo_path, exc). Optionally count failures in a metrics dict returned for forensics.

findings.title: Magic ratio 0.75 inline despite docstring explanation
findings.description: The guard replacement threshold is hardcoded as `removed * 0.75` while historical_rag.py uses named constants (_MIN_CLASSIFIED_FOR_KNN). Docstring explains the ratio but the value is not a module-level named constant, making tuning and cross-reference harder and violating project DRY/naming conventions.
findings.fix: Extract `_GUARD_REPLACEMENT_RATIO = 0.75` with a one-line comment citing empirically balanced refactoring fixture (TestNetGuardRemoval). Use in return statement.

findings.title: Lazy import inside per-commit hot path
findings.description: Import of get_historical_defect_context is inside build_investigation_messages(), called once per commit in batch eval. Python caches sys.modules so cost is negligible after first call, but it violates import hygiene used elsewhere in the module, obscures the dependency graph, and pairs with try/except to hide ImportError.
findings.fix: Move to module-level import with optional try/except at import time setting a HAS_H3A flag, or unconditional import since historical_rag is part of the package.

findings.title: Systematic stride sampling is chronologically biased
findings.description: project_rows[::step][:sample_size] samples every Nth row in CSV iteration order (likely temporal), not randomly. Early-project defect distributions may dominate fallback priors; recent bug patterns underrepresented. Documented as 'evenly' but that describes stride spacing, not statistical representativeness.
findings.fix: Use random.sample with fixed seed for reproducibility, or stratify by time quantile. Document bias if stride kept for performance.

findings.title: First-match-wins taxonomy ordering causes misclassification
findings.description: Categories are checked in fixed list order; broad patterns in error-handling and configuration (e.g. \bversion\b, \bdependency\b, \bfail\b) match before narrower categories. A 'fix null pointer on config load' message becomes null-dereference (correct) but 'fix dependency version causing timeout' may become error-handling instead of configuration or api-contract.
findings.fix: Document precedence rules in module docstring; add tests for ambiguous messages; consider scoring all matches and picking highest-specificity category.

findings.title: Fallback path misreports fetched count in source label
findings.description: When using project-level fallback, code sets `fetched = total_classified` (approximate for display). The source label then claims 'N similar commits' semantics are wrong — undermines trust in injected prior provenance shown to the LLM.
findings.fix: Use separate variables: knn_fetched vs fallback_sample_size. Label string should say 'project-wide base rate from M sampled commits' without conflating counts.

findings.title: Test path regex may miss non-Maven test layouts
findings.description: _TEST_FILE_RE requires `/test/` in path or specific suffixes (Test.java). Layouts like `tests/unit/Foo_test.py` or `src/tests/` without `/test/` segment won't qualify for test-only exemption, causing false defect signals on test-only commits in non-Java repos.
findings.fix: Audit touched_files from n50 eval for false negatives. Extend pattern with `^tests/` and `_test.py$` if data supports it.

findings.title: Module exceeds 300-line project sizing guideline
findings.description: historical_rag.py combines taxonomy, CSV loading, KNN, git I/O, and formatting in one file. Not blocking but increases review burden.
findings.fix: Split into historical_rag/taxonomy.py and historical_rag/lookup.py when adding tests.

findings.title: hypothesis_engine.py exceeds 300-line sizing guideline
findings.description: Pre-existing sizing debt; H3a block adds coupling in an already large module.

findings.title: Guard counting uses regex findall line matches not semantic guard units
findings.description: removed/added counts are len(findall) on +/- lines, not distinct guard sites. A single line with multiple null checks counts once; conversely duplicate hunks in merged diffs could inflate counts. Acceptable heuristic but boundary at 0.75 ratio is fragile.
findings.fix: Document limitation in docstring. Optional: count unique matched line hashes for stability.
